text: Writing clean code is an important skill for every programmer. Clean code is easy to read and understand, even for someone who did not write it. One key idea is using clear naming conventions, so variables and functions have names that explain what they do. For example, a function called "calculateTotal" is much better than one called "calc." Another important point is keeping functions small and focused on a single task. This makes the code simpler to test and fix. Finally, clean code is easier to maintain over time. When you or your teammates return to the project later, readable code saves hours of confusion and prevents mistakes.
